# Discussion Board Project Overview

## Purpose

The discussion board project aims to create a robust, flexible, and scalable online platform for communities to collaborate, communicate, and engage in meaningful conversations. By offering a centralized space for discussions, this system brings together stakeholders, customers, and interest groups, enhancing knowledge sharing and driving constructive engagement. The platform is designed to fulfill the needs of modern organizations, educational institutions, interest-based communities, and support environments.

## Strategic Objectives

- **Enable Open Discussions:** THE system SHALL facilitate persistent, topic-centered conversations among users.
- **Promote Safe and Inclusive Participation:** THE system SHALL enforce community guidelines to foster respectful and welcoming interactions at all times.
- **Support Engagement and Collaboration:** THE system SHALL provide intuitive tools for users to contribute, react, and build upon existing conversations.
- **Ensure Accessibility and Availability:** THE system SHALL support seamless access across devices, ensuring high availability and usability for diverse user groups.

## Target Audiences

- **Enterprise Teams:** In-house discussion, project collaboration, cross-departmental feedback.
- **Educational Institutions:** Classroom Q&A, student forums, faculty-student engagement.
- **Interest Communities:** Hobby groups, open source collaborators, volunteers, and professional networks.
- **Customer Support:** User-generated FAQ, service discussion, troubleshooting, and knowledge base expansion.

## User Roles and Value Propositions

- **Administrators:** Obtain comprehensive controls to configure the board, manage users and content, enforce moderation policy, and maintain system health.
- **Moderators:** Possess efficient tools for content oversight, spam management, and enforcing community guidelines.
- **Members:** Benefit from rich posting, commenting, voting, and content discovery experiences, enhancing personal and group participation.
- **Guests:** Enjoy an open gateway to browse public discussions, discover trending topics, and become future contributors.

## Key Features Overview

- Persistent topic threads and nested discussions
- Comprehensive search capabilities
- Voting and reputation mechanism to surface valuable content
- Real-time notifications on tracked discussions or followed topics
- Reporting and moderation tools for managing unwanted behavior
- Customizable categories, tags, and access permissions
- Content safety and data privacy by design
- Activity insights and analytics

## Use Cases

- WHEN a team starts a new initiative, THE system SHALL provide a dedicated space for ongoing conversation.
- WHEN a user seeks help, THE system SHALL connect them to a community of experts and peers via public Q&A.
- WHEN a controversial topic emerges, THE system SHALL support transparent moderation and escalation workflows.

## Implementation Principles

- THE system SHALL be modular to accommodate future expansion and third-party integrations.
- THE system SHALL deliver responsive UX/UI for optimal engagement on web and mobile platforms.
- THE system SHALL maintain data integrity, support legal compliance, and uphold the highest security standards.

## Success Criteria

- Measurable growth in active users and engagement rates within three months of launch
- High user satisfaction based on regular feedback cycles and analytics
- Positive moderation outcomes with minimal incident escalation
- Sustainable and adaptable architecture supporting evolving community needs

# Discussion Board User Roles and Permissions

## Overview
This document defines the roles, permissions, and access responsibilities for the Discussion Board system. It outlines each user role’s allowed actions, restrictions, responsibilities, and any relevant conditions driving permission enforcement. Details are structured for maximum clarity and self-sufficiency, suitable for system implementation and test-case derivation.

## Defined User Roles

### 1. Admin
Admins have full management access across the board, including configuration and user control.

#### Permissions and Responsibilities
- THE system SHALL allow admins to perform all moderator, member, and guest actions.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to create, modify, or delete any post, comment, or thread.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to manage user roles (assign, revoke, or modify permissions).
- THE system SHALL allow admins to suspend, ban, or reinstate user accounts immediately.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to configure category structures and discussion settings.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to access and export all board data, including analytics, logs, and user activity histories.
- IF an action is restricted to other roles, THEN THE system SHALL allow admins to override all such restrictions.

### 2. Moderator
Moderators provide rule enforcement and content management but lack access to system-wide settings.

#### Permissions and Responsibilities
- THE system SHALL allow moderators to delete, edit, or move posts and comments not created by themselves when such posts violate board policies.
- THE system SHALL allow moderators to review, act on, and resolve user reports.
- THE system SHALL allow moderators to suspend or temporarily mute accounts except for admins.
- THE system SHALL NOT grant moderators access to system configuration, category structure, or analytics export functions.
- Moderators SHALL NOT promote or demote users to or from the admin role.

### 3. Member
Authenticated users who contribute content and interact with community features.

#### Permissions and Responsibilities
- WHEN a member is authenticated, THE system SHALL allow them to create, edit, or delete their own posts and comments.
- THE system SHALL allow members to upvote, downvote, or report other user content.
- THE system SHALL allow members to access private or member-only categories.
- IF a member attempts an action beyond their scope (e.g., deleting another user's post), THEN THE system SHALL deny the request and display an appropriate message.

### 4. Guest
Unauthenticated or non-registered users with minimal access.

#### Permissions and Responsibilities
- THE system SHALL allow guests to browse public discussion categories and read posts.
- THE system SHALL restrict guests from posting, commenting, or voting within any category.
- THE system SHALL display post counts, trending topics, and publicly-available statistics to guests.
- THE system SHALL NOT grant guests access to private or restricted categories.

## Role Change and Permission Update Conditions
- WHEN a user role is changed by an authorized admin, THE system SHALL enforce the new permissions immediately without delay.
- IF a user session’s token is invalid, expired, or missing, THEN THE system SHALL treat the user as a guest until re-authentication occurs.

## General Principles
- THE system SHALL enforce least-privilege logic for all role types at every endpoint and UX element.
- ALL permission and authentication-related requirements SHALL be captured here and directly implemented without referencing external access control documents.

---
*For reference to role definitions in API endpoints or access logic, see the roles outlined above.*

# Discussion Board Feature and Workflow Specification

## Overview
The Discussion Board service enables users to interact by posting content, commenting on discussions, voting on contributions, and participating in moderated conversations. This document specifies all core features and workflows, ensuring independent usability for developers and stakeholders.

---

## 1. Posting and Thread Management
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL allow members to create text-based or multimedia posts within their permitted categories.
- **Event-driven:** WHEN a member submits a new post, THE system SHALL validate the input, assign it a unique identifier, timestamp it, and associate it with the author’s profile.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL display posts in reverse chronological order by default, with filtering and sorting options available.
- **Event-driven:** WHEN a post is edited or deleted by its author, THE system SHALL update or remove the content and maintain an audit trail accessible to moderators and admins.

---

## 2. Commenting and Threaded Replies
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL support hierarchical (threaded) comments on posts and existing comments.
- **Event-driven:** WHEN a member submits a comment, THE system SHALL validate and attach it to the corresponding post or comment.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL permit members to edit or delete their own comments, triggering audit logging for moderation purposes.

---

## 3. Voting and Engagement
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL provide upvote and downvote options on posts and comments for authenticated users.
- **Unwanted Behavior:** IF a user attempts to vote more than once on the same item, THEN THE system SHALL reject the duplicate vote and notify the user.
- **State-driven:** WHILE displaying posts or comments, THE system SHALL show aggregated vote counts and trending indicators.

---

## 4. Moderation and Reporting
- **Event-driven:** WHEN a member flags a post or comment for review, THE system SHALL record the report, generate a notification for moderators, and mark the content as pending review.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL enable moderators to edit, delete, or suspend content and user accounts as outlined by defined roles.
- **Unwanted Behavior:** IF content violates board policies, THEN THE system SHALL escalate to an admin for final action.

---

## 5. Registration, Authentication, and Roles
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL allow guest browsing of public sections but restrict posting, voting, or reporting to authenticated members.
- **Event-driven:** WHEN a guest attempts to use restricted features, THE system SHALL redirect to the registration or login flow.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL assign roles (admin, moderator, member, guest) with permissions enforced for all operations.

---

## 6. Notifications and User Feedback
- **Event-driven:** WHEN users receive replies, votes, or moderation actions on their content, THE system SHALL generate and deliver in-app or email notifications according to user settings.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL clearly display system status messages (e.g., success, errors, moderation outcomes) after member actions.

---

## 7. Accessibility and Usability
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL adhere to accessibility standards (WCAG 2.1 AA) to ensure usability for all users.
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL provide help tooltips and contextual guidance for major actions (posting, voting, reporting).

---

## 8. Data Integrity and Auditability
- **Ubiquitous:** THE system SHALL maintain an immutable audit log of all content creation, edits, deletions, voting, and moderation events.
- **Unwanted Behavior:** IF data corruption or unauthorized access is detected, THEN THE system SHALL alert admins and initiate mitigations automatically.

---

## 9. Acceptance Criteria
- All user-visible features described above are present in the UI and function as specified.
- Role-based access control prevents unauthorized actions.
- Moderation tools allow effective handling of reports and violations.
- Audit logs and notifications operate consistently across relevant actions.

---

## End of Document

# Discussion Board API Authentication & Access Control

---

## Table of Contents
1. Overview
2. Authentication Overview
3. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
4. API Endpoint Access Matrix
5. Authentication and Authorization Flows
6. Security & Compliance Considerations
7. Acceptance Criteria

---

## 1. Overview
This document details the API-centric authentication and authorization system for the discussion board platform. It uses role-based access control (RBAC) for four roles: admin, moderator, member, and guest. EARS-based requirements are deployed throughout.

---

## 2. Authentication Overview
- THE API SHALL support JWT-based authentication for member, moderator, and admin roles.
- WHEN a user issues login credentials to the API, THE API SHALL validate them and issue a signed token on success.
- IF an authentication token is expired or invalid, THEN THE API SHALL reject the request with an appropriate error.
- WHERE the user is a guest, THE API SHALL allow limited unauthenticated access with restricted endpoints.

---

## 3. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
| Role       | Description                                         |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Admin      | Full access; system configuration and exports       |
| Moderator  | Moderation powers, no system setting rights         |
| Member     | Authenticated user; create/edit content             |
| Guest      | Unauthenticated; can browse selected endpoints      |

- THE API SHALL enforce role permissions at the endpoint and business logic layers.

---

## 4. API Endpoint Access Matrix
| Endpoint                | Admin | Moderator | Member | Guest |
|-------------------------|:-----:|:---------:|:------:|:-----:|
| /posts                  |  RW   |    RW     |  RW    |   R   |
| /posts/:id              |  RW   |    RW     |  RW    |   R   |
| /comments               |  RW   |    RW     |  RW    |   R   |
| /users                  |  RW   |   View    |  View  |   -   |
| /moderation/reports     |  RW   |    RW     |   -    |   -   |
| /admin/settings         |  RW   |     -     |   -    |   -   |

*R: Read, W: Write, RW: Read & Write*

---

## 5. Authentication & Authorization Flows
### 5.1 Login/Token Issuance
- WHEN a user provides valid credentials, THE API SHALL return an access token.
- WHEN credentials are invalid, THE API SHALL return an 'Unauthorized' error.
- WHILE the access token is valid, THE API SHALL allow actions according to the user's role.

### 5.2 Token Validation Middleware
- THE API SHALL use authentication middleware to validate all requests except those designated as public.

### 5.3 Guest Access
- IF no valid token is supplied, THEN THE API SHALL treat the user as Guest and restrict actions appropriately.

### 5.4 Role Checks
- WHEN an endpoint requires elevated permissions, THE API SHALL check the user's role before granting access.

---

## 6. Security & Compliance Considerations
- THE API SHALL use encrypted (HTTPS) communication for all endpoints.
- WHEN multi-factor authentication is enabled, THE API SHALL require additional verification during login.
- IF repeated invalid authentication attempts occur, THEN THE API SHALL implement rate limiting or account lockout measures.
- THE API SHALL log all access and modification actions made by privileged roles for auditability.

---

## 7. Acceptance Criteria
- Authentication tokens are strictly required for all non-guest operations.
- Each role is granted only the minimal necessary privileges for its endpoints.
- Unauthorized access attempts are logged and rejected with correct error codes.
- All requirements above are written and testable in EARS format.

# Content Moderation and Policy Handling

## Overview
This document defines the comprehensive framework and operational requirements for content moderation, abuse reporting, escalation procedures, and policy enforcement within the Discussion Board system. It provides a self-contained reference for all aspects of ensuring safe, respectful, and policy-compliant interactions among all user roles, independent of other documents.

## Content Moderation Objectives
- Ensure community guideline compliance across all posts, comments, and user-generated content
- Enable prompt identification, review, and resolution of violations
- Protect users from unlawful, harassing, or disruptive behavior
- Support transparent, consistent, and accountable moderator actions

## Moderation Roles and Responsibilities
| Role        | Responsibilities                                                                                          |
|-------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| admin       | Final decision on escalated content, oversight of policy settings, audit all moderation actions           |
| moderator   | Review and act on reports, delete/edit posts, suspend users within set guidelines, escalate severe cases   |
| member      | Report inappropriate content, appeal moderation actions, comply with posting standards                    |
| guest       | View/report public violations; limited action capabilities                                                |

## Moderation Requirements (EARS)
- THE system SHALL provide moderators with tools to review, edit, delete, or restore posts and comments.
- WHEN content is reported, THE system SHALL flag it for moderator review.
- IF a moderator acts on content, THEN THE system SHALL log the action with timestamp, actor, and rationale.
- IF flagged content is urgent/severe, THEN THE system SHALL prioritize review in moderator queues.
- WHERE user appeals occur, THE system SHALL allow admins to audit and override moderator decisions.
- WHILE a user is suspended, THE system SHALL prevent new posts/comments from that user.
- WHEN policy updates are made, THE system SHALL notify all moderators and relevant stakeholders.

## Abuse Reporting Workflow
1. **Reporting:** All logged-in users and guests may report posts/comments for potential violations.
2. **Categorization:** System prompts reporter to specify violation type (harassment, spam, illegal content, etc.).
3. **Flagging:** Reported content is flagged and made visible in moderator dashboards.
4. **Initial Review:** Moderator reviews flagged content, evidence, and event logs.
5. **Action:** Possible actions: dismiss, edit, delete, user suspension, escalation to admin.
6. **Logging:** All steps are audit-logged for accountability.

## Escalation and Policy Enforcement
- THE system SHALL automatically escalate repeated or severe violations to admin for review.
- WHEN an action results in user suspension/ban, THE system SHALL notify affected users with reason and duration.
- IF content is part of ongoing legal investigation, THEN THE system SHALL restrict access pending outcome.
- WHERE local laws require, THE system SHALL provide data export for enforcement agencies upon appropriate request.

## Edge Cases and Exceptions
- IF multiple conflicting reports exist, THEN THE system SHALL require joint moderator/admin review before decision.
- WHEN policy ambiguities are detected, THE system SHALL mark for policy team clarification and show interim guidance.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All moderator actions are fully traceable and reversible (audit trail maintained for minimum 12 months)
- No unreviewed flagged content remains in the system longer than maximum review time (e.g., 48 hours)
- Policy changes are time-stamped and all relevant parties informed within 24 hours
- False-positive handling: Appeals reviewed by higher authority; decision feedback provided within 3 days

## Revision History
- 2025-08-04: Initial, fully self-contained version for review.

This model enables separation of discussion spaces for workflow and access control, mapping category names to public/posting/finding/review requirements. Maintains 3NF as all values are atomic and not derived. Example: 'Help', 'Announcements', 'General'. Key relationships: Many posts belong to a category; tags assigned via category_tags. ### `discussion_board_categories`

Category definitions - Implements the business requirement for persistent, configurable categorized discussion areas (Feature 1, Posting/Thread Management, and project objectives). This model enables separation of discussion spaces for workflow and access control, mapping category names to public/posting/finding/review requirements. Maintains 3NF as all values are atomic and not derived. Example: 'Help', 'Announcements', 'General'. Key relationships: Many posts belong to a category; tags assigned via category_tags. Special behaviors: Name must be unique, soft deletion allowed, audit trail via timestamps.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`: Category name - uniquely identifies the category as required for post/thread assignment and category configuration. Maintains normalization by being atomic and single-purpose. Used in category selectors, post creation, audit logs, moderation workflows. Must be unique.
- `description`: Optional description for category - guides admins and users about the category’s purpose. Null allowed for concise categories, maintains 3NF by only referencing this category. Used in UI help/tooltips.
- `created_at`: Category creation timestamp - implements audit and compliance requirements for traceability. Maintains normalization as atomic event log. Used for sorting/filtering, admin review, audit logs.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for last admin modification - maps to admin/audit requirements for configuration changes. Used in admin UIs, audit trails, compliance routines. Maintains 3NF.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion (if the category is deleted but should remain for policy/history). Maintains normalization as atomic value and complies with audit/recovery requirements. Used in policy enforcement, safe removes, and potential category restoration. Nullable.

### `discussion_board_tags`

Tag definitions - Implements tagging and flexible content categorization requirements (referenced in project overview, feature spec, usability/accessibility). Enables UIs and admin policies for discoverability, faceted navigation, and access control. Maintains 3NF with atomic, non-derived values. Example: 'urgent', 'release', 'staff'. Relationships: Assigned to categories via category_tags; may be assigned to posts/comments elsewhere. Special behaviors: 'label' must be unique, soft deletion for compliance/audit, optional color for UI display.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `label`: Short text label for the tag - enables tagging UI, content filtering, and administrative assignment. Atomic and normalized; uniquely identifies tag for assignment. Used in create/search/sort navigation. Must be unique.
- `description`: Optional description for this tag - displayed to admins or users for clarity. Maintains 3NF as atomic, non-derived value. Nullable for lightweight tags.
- `color`: Tag color code (HTML hex or class) for display/UI cues - implements branding/accessibility. Normalized as atomic attribute, not required. Nullable.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp, for administrative/audit trail compliance and tag lifecycle management. Non-nullable, atomic, and normalized. Used in filtering/audit.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for admin modifications (e.g., label, color) to this tag. Implements audit traceability and admin compliance. Used in change logging and admin review.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp marking tag as soft-deleted (if ever removed for compliance/policy). Supports safe deletion/feature-recovery as per requirements. Nullable; maintains normalization.

### `discussion_board_category_tags`

Junction: Category/Tag assignment - Implements flexible M:N category x tag linkage required for configurable board structure (allowing each category to have multiple tags and each tag to apply to multiple categories). Fulfills normalized structure by storing only category-tag pairs; no derived or aggregate fields present. Example usage: associating 'urgent' with 'Help', 'release' with 'Announcements'. Key relationships: Many-to-one to discussion_board_categories and discussion_board_tags. Special behaviors: Composite uniqueness of (category, tag), assignment timestamp for audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `discussion_board_category_id`: Linked category's id - foreign key to [discussion_board_categories.id](#discussion_board_categories). Implements requirement for linking categories to tags via junction. Not unique, required.
- `discussion_board_tag_id`: Linked tag's id - foreign key to [discussion_board_tags.id](#discussion_board_tags). Allows assignment of tags to categories. Not unique, required.
- `created_at`: Assignment timestamp for when this tag was linked to this category. Atomic event for audit/compliance; maintains 3NF.

### `discussion_board_board_settings`

Board/global configuration - Implements requirement for systematic, single-source, board-level settings and branding (project overview, admin permissions, setup, and configuration features). All fields are atomic and not derived, supporting complete normalization for configuration data. Example: board title/configuration for branding or policy. Relationships: not referenced by other domains as FK. Special behaviors: Typically single-row; optional logo/support for branding; enabled/disabled toggling for maintenance. All configuration edits recorded via updated_at.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key (expected single-row only).
- `title`: Board title for branding and user-facing display. Implements requirement for customizable system header/branding. Maintains normalization as atomic attribute. Used in UI, welcome screens.
- `description`: Optional board description shown on landing pages and board information modals. Implements requirement for user guidance and compliance context. Nullable, atomic.
- `enabled`: Whether this board is active/enabled (vs. offline/maintenance). Implements admin control requirement for access/mode. Used to survive maintenance/disable in a single config place. Atomic, mapped 1:1 to admin toggle.
- `logo_uri`: Optional logo image (display URI). Implements branding/config requirement for admins; nullable for minimalist boards; maintains 3NF as atomic value.
- `created_at`: When this board setup/config record was created. Implements system audit and admin requirements for setup history. Used during operations/audit.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for last configuration update/change. Maintains full normalization as atomic value and supports requirement for admin audit/rollback.

### `discussion_board_admins`

Explicit administrator account model - This implements the requirement for explicit admin role (see Roles and Permissions doc). Enables granular access control, permission enforcement, and auditability for administrator actions. 3NF normalization: business fields atomic (username, password_hash, email), no calculated values. Used for authentication, role assignment, and audit tracking. Key relationships: referenced by moderator promotions, moderation records. Special behaviors: username/email uniqueness and active flag enforcement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `username`: Admin's unique username used for authentication and audit tracking. Implements explicit admin identity, mapped to the Roles and Permissions requirement. Each admin must have an immutable, account-unique name.
- `password_hash`: Secure password hash (not plaintext) for authentication. Implements security and data integrity requirement. No business logic outside authentication.
- `email`: Admin's business email. Implements requirement for notification and account recovery. Uniqueness ensures clear identity reference.
- `is_active`: Whether this admin account is currently authorized. Requirement: immediate permission enforcement upon promotion/suspension.
- `created_at`: Timestamp marking admin account creation. Requirement: audit trail/auditability; supports analytics.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for admin account. Implements audit trail and policy updates requirement for traceability.

### `discussion_board_moderators`

Moderator account with explicit separation from admin and member roles - Implements moderator-specific requirements (see Roles and Permissions, Moderation Policy). Maintains normalized role boundaries; supports permission enforcement and audit-log promotion tracking. Used for authentication, access, and audit logs. Key relationships: references discussion_board_admins by promoted_by_admin_id. 3NF enforced. Special behaviors: account activation and promotion traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `promoted_by_admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who last promoted this moderator. Enables audit-trail and RBAC traceability.
- `username`: Moderator's username used for login and unique session. Implements moderator identity, not shared with admins.
- `password_hash`: Moderator's secure password hash for authentication. Implements security and data integrity requirement.
- `email`: Moderator's email for communication and notification purposes.
- `is_active`: Current active status for this moderator (permission enforcement).
- `created_at`: Account creation timestamp for auditability/tracking.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp for moderator account.

### `discussion_board_members`

Member account table for authenticated content contributors - Implements member role separation and audit requirements from Feature Spec and Roles doc. Supports atomic member-only fields: display_name, email, password, is_verified, status, last_login_at. Used for board participation, access control, and behavioral analytics. 3NF normalization ensures all fields atomic, no calculated aggregates. Key relationships: referenced by content, moderation, and notification tables. Special behavior: verification and permission status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `display_name`: Display name for UI and participant identification. Implements member identity requirement. Must be unique per member for display purposes, not system-unique.
- `email`: Member's email for notifications and authentication. Implements communication and uniqueness constraint requirement.
- `password_hash`: Password hash (not plaintext); authentication only.
- `is_verified`: Whether member is verified (e.g. email confirmed); permission escalation requirement.
- `registered_at`: Member registration timestamp for audit trail and analytics.
- `status`: Current permission status of member (active, suspended, banned). Implements immediate enforcement requirement.
- `last_login_at`: Timestamp of last login (nullable). For analytics and re-engagement. Null if never logged in.

### `discussion_board_guests`

Guest session/account representation - Implements requirements for guests to have visible, minimally tracked presence (for access, audit, and deduplication only). Contains only atomic data: id (session UUID), guest_ip (for minimal audit), session_token (for deduplication not authentication), entered_at. Used by content and access domains for logging and abuse detection. 3NF ensured, no account-linkage or calculated fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `guest_ip`: IP address for guest identification. Requirement: minimal audit-trail for legal/compliance.
- `session_token`: Session-specific identifier or browser fingerprint. For deduplication only.
- `entered_at`: Timestamp when guest first entered (session start time). Analytics and tracking.

### `discussion_board_posts`

Discussion board posts entity - This implements the core posting and thread management requirements from the requirements document. Business purpose: to store user-created posts, support nesting for threaded discussions, maintain ownership attribution via member links, and provide edit/delete auditability via history relationships. Maintains strict 3NF normalization by making all data atomic and referencing other entities via foreign keys only. For example, posts can be filtered by category/tag, searched by content, or linked to moderation workflows. Key relationships: belongs to a member (author), may have parent (for threading), linked to tags/categories (junctions), has comments, votes, and full edit audit trail. Special behaviors: soft deletion, GIN index for full-text search, multi-level hierarchy via parent_id.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Implements the requirement for uniquely identifiable posts while supporting audit, edit/delete traceability, and hierarchical structuring for discussions.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Author of the post - references existing discussion_board_members table. Implements user attribution for all posting activity. Normalization: 3NF enforced.
- `parent_id`: Self-referencing field to enable nested/threaded posts. Nullable for top-level posts. 3NF normalization: only atomic reference; rest of parent data never duplicated.
- `title`: Title of the post - Implements requirement for user-generated summaries and search. Atomic, supports full-text search GIN. No calculation, pure data.
- `body`: Main content/body of the post. Implements requirement for persistent, rich-text discussions. Normalized single value, no calculation.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for post creation. Implements audit, moderation, and chronology requirements. Atomic, not calculated.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp to enable audit trails and moderation transparency. 3NF normalized.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for moderation, audit, and reporting. Null means active; non-null means deleted (soft). Enforces requirement for reversible deletions/audits.

### `discussion_board_comments`

Discussion comments entity - Implements threaded/hierarchical comment requirement, auditable histories, post association, and edit/deletion tracking. Business purpose: to attach persistent, atomic user comments to posts or to other comments (threaded). Strict 3NF normalization maintained throughout. For example, member creates comment, which can be replied to, edited, deleted, and voted on. Relationships: belongs to member (author), links to post, may have parent comment (threading), and edit/vote audit histories. Special: GIN index on content for search, soft deletion for moderation traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each comment, supporting full audit, reporting, and threading. 3NF.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Author of the comment - references existing discussion_board_members table. Needed for audit, reporting, moderation. 3NF enforced.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Attached post. References existing discussion_board_posts. Requirement: all comments tied to a post. Normalized, atomic reference.
- `parent_id`: Self-referencing optional parent comment to allow threaded replies. Null for top-level comments. 3NF: atomic reference, zero duplication.
- `body`: Comment text for discussions. Implements core requirement for comments, normalized, atomic value.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for audit, moderation, and reporting; complies with audit/auditability requirements. Not a calculation.
- `updated_at`: Audit requirement for edit history; supports transparency and accountability. Normalized date field.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if active, else denotes deletion for moderation reporting/audit. Normalized atomic value.

### `discussion_board_post_votes`

Post voting entity - Implements requirement for voting (up/down) on posts. 3NF enforcement (atomic, no calculations in post table). All individual votes are traceable to both post and member per requirements. Business: supports engagement metrics, moderation, and audit. Usage: ensures only one vote per member per post (unique index).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. One record per vote event, ensuring full normalization, auditable voting histories with no redundancy. 3NF.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Post being voted on, references discussion_board_posts. Atomic, normalized reference.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Voting member - references discussion_board_members. 3NF enforced; enables full audit, traceability, unique vote enforcement.
- `upvote`: Vote type (up=true, down=false). Supports engagement/reputation, normalized, atomic.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for vote event for audit and analytics; atomic field.

### `discussion_board_comment_votes`

Comment voting entity - Fulfills requirement for upvotes/downvotes (atomic) on comments with auditability. Each record links to both comment and voting member; unique index enforces one vote per user per comment. Audit-friendly, strictly 3NF (no aggregate/calculated fields).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. One record per vote on a comment. Supports analytic requirements and audit trails. 3NF.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`: Voted comment. References discussion_board_comments; supports moderation and audit.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: Voting member - references discussion_board_members. 1:N member-to-votes. Unique constraint for 1 vote per comment per user.
- `upvote`: Vote polarity. Upvote=true, downvote=false. Atomic, normalized, directly mapped to requirements.
- `created_at`: Vote timestamp for audit, reporting, compliance. Normalized atomic value.

### `discussion_board_post_tags`

Junction table for post-tag connections - Implements requirement for flexible post tagging with normalized, atomic entity representing each post-tag relationship. Supports filtering, analytics, and reporting with zero redundancy (enforces 3NF). For example, find all posts for a tag or all tags for a post by querying this table. Key: Each post-tag pair appears at most once (unique constraint).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Each post-tag pair as a separate record enforces 3NF and supports analytics, filtering. Implements junction requirement for flexible tagging.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: FK to post in relationship. Atomic field, enforces single post per junction.
- `discussion_board_tag_id`: FK to tag (Systematic). Normalized atomic field, supports tag lists and filter/search features across posts.

### `discussion_board_post_categories`

Junction table for post-category relationships - Implements the flexible post categorization required in the requirements document. Each record maps a post to a category (from Systematic) in 3NF. No denormalization, pure linking. Example: supports filtering, analytics, reporting, and browsing by category. Unique constraint ensures no duplicates for the same post-category pair.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Each post-category pair as atomic record (junction table). 3NF; future-proofs reporting, filtering requirements.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: FK to post entity. Maintains atomic reference for N:M relationship.
- `discussion_board_category_id`: FK to category (from Systematic tables). Assignment supports flexible browsing, analytics, and reporting. Strict normalization: category information never duplicated.

### `discussion_board_comment_edits`

Comment edit audit/entity - Implements the full audit trail requirement for comment changes, both voluntary and moderation-driven. Each record represents a normalized atomic edit, fully traceable and reversible. Supports compliance, reporting, and transparency (e.g., reconstruct full edit history). For example, moderator can view all changes to a comment or revert if needed. Key relationships: links to comment, editor (member). 3NF enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Each comment edit event as atomic record for full audit traceability, supporting both voluntary and moderation edits. 3NF.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`: FK to comment entity, supports 1:N edit history structure. Normalized atomic field.
- `discussion_board_member_id`: FK to member (editor of comment). Enforced by requirements for edit/revert visibility and auditability (3NF).
- `new_body`: The new text content after the edit event. Implements edit/audit requirement as atomic value. No calculation or transformation stored.
- `edited_at`: Timestamp for the edit, providing full traceability for audit, moderation, and forensics. Normalization enforced.
- `rationale`: Rationale for the edit; optional field to support transparency and compliance. Atomic field; null if not provided.

### `discussion_board_post_edits`

Post edit audit/entity - Implements full edit and moderation audit trail requirement from the requirements document. Each record captures one edit event (atomic), supports reversibility, and provides accountability for changes. Enables transparent audit trails for both members and moderators. Usage: e.g., reconstruct edit history for a given post, query rationale for changes. Relationships: links to post, editor (member); 3NF enforced.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Each post edit event as separate record. 3NF and full requirements mapping for audit.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: FK to post (being edited). Atomic, supports edit history (1:N).
- `discussion_board_member_id`: FK to editor (member). Attribution for edit history, compliance, undo/revert history; 3NF and transparent business logic.
- `new_title`: New title for post (if changed in edit). Nullable, atomic, no redundancy or calculation. 3NF preserved.
- `new_body`: New body for post (if applicable in edit event). Nullable, atomic, normalized (never calculated or derived).

### `discussion_board_content_reports`

Tracks all user/content abuse reports. This implements the moderation and policy enforcement requirements from the requirement spec. Business purpose: capture and process actionable abuse/violation reports for posts and comments. Fully normalized (3NF): each report references atomic user/content, with categorical and status metadata. Use cases include triggering moderation workflows and supporting audit/review cycles. Related to actors (reporter) and content tables. Special behaviors: immutable after creation except for status updates/resolution.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - unique identifier for each moderation report.
- `reporter_admin_id`: Reporter admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if reporter is an admin.
- `reporter_moderator_id`: Reporter moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if reporter is a moderator.
- `reporter_member_id`: Reporter member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if reporter is a member.
- `reporter_guest_id`: Reporter guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if reporter is a guest.
- `discussion_board_post_id`: Target post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts) if report is about a post (nullable). Use together with content_type = 'post'.
- `discussion_board_comment_id`: Target comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments) if report is about a comment (nullable). Use together with content_type = 'comment'.
- `content_type`: Type of content ('post' or 'comment'). Implements type discrimination for reference integrity.
- `category`: Report reason category (policy, spam, offensive, etc.).
- `reason`: Human-readable reason provided for moderation review/audit.
- `status`: Current status (e.g., pending, under_review, resolved, dismissed) for moderation/workflow tracking.
- `reported_at`: ISO timestamp for report filing (audit/compliance requirement).
- `resolved_at`: Timestamp for when report is resolved (nullable if pending/under_review).

### `discussion_board_moderation_actions`

Stores all moderation actions (edit, delete, escalate, suspend, etc.) that arise as a result of reports or proactive moderation. Implements the moderation workflow, audit trail, and accountability requirements. 3NF: Each action references an atomic report and actor, descriptive type and timestamps. Usage: Drives ban, delete, escalation, and appeal handling. Related to content_reports and actors. Special behaviors: Actions are mutable only for correction by designated actors and are permanently audit-logged.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - unique identifier for each moderation action.
- `report_id`: Moderation action targets a discussion_board_content_reports entry.
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) executing the moderation action (nullable if actor is a moderator).
- `moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) executing the moderation action (nullable if actor is an admin).
- `action_type`: Type of moderation action (edit, suspend, escalate, etc.). Implements requirement for workflow tracking.
- `description`: Business/log reason for action; provides compliance with transparency policy.
- `acted_at`: ISO timestamp for action (immutable, for audit trail).

### `discussion_board_appeals`

Tracks user appeals to moderation actions/decisions. Implements business rules around escalation and fair review. Fully normalized and auditable: each appeal atomically references a single action, appellant, and audit timestamps. Used for workflow lifecycle and regulator tracing. Related to moderation_actions and actors (appellant). Special behaviors: Unique per (action_id, appellant_id) to prevent repeated appeals for same event.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - each appeal event.
- `action_id`: FK to moderation_action being appealed.
- `appellant_admin_id`: Appellant admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if appellant is an admin.
- `appellant_moderator_id`: Appellant moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if appellant is a moderator.
- `appellant_member_id`: Appellant member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if appellant is a member.
- `appellant_guest_id`: Appellant guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if appellant is a guest.
- `reason`: Appellant's justification/rationale for the appeal.
- `status`: Appeal status (pending/approved/denied). For business rule lifecycle.
- `submitted_at`: Appeal submitted at (audit/fair review log).
- `resolved_at`: Appeal resolution timestamp (nullable until acted).

### `discussion_board_suspensions`

Tracks each instance of a user suspension or ban. Implements business logic for lockout, temporary or permanent bans. 3NF: Each row refers to a single actor and the moderator/admin imposing the suspension. Suspension state/status is atomic. Related report/action links optionally. Used in enforcement, audit, and reporting. Special behaviors: indexed by suspended_user_id and start time for efficient user lookup and reversal.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - suspension or ban event log.
- `suspended_admin_id`: Suspended admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if banned user is an admin.
- `suspended_moderator_id`: Suspended moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if banned user is a moderator.
- `suspended_member_id`: Suspended member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if banned user is a member.
- `suspended_guest_id`: Suspended guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if banned user is a guest.
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who imposed the suspension.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) who imposed the suspension.
- `related_report_id`: Related abuse report (nullable).
- `related_action_id`: Related moderation action (nullable).
- `suspended_at`: Suspension start timestamp. Enforces audit/lockout state evolutions.
- `ends_at`: Suspension end (nullable for indefinite). For permanent/temporary logic.
- `reason`: Admin/moderator reason for suspension (audit/business policy transparency).
- `status`: Suspension status (active/expired/revoked). Used for lookup and reporting.

### `discussion_board_audit_logs`

Immutable log of all moderation domain actions, implementing regulatory and business requirement for activity auditability. 3NF, strictly atomic fields. Each log entry links to a moderation action, actor, and redundant action_type for query. Used for reporting, legal compliance, and restore/escalation logic. Special: context nullable for differential audit detail by business process.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - immutable audit log entry.
- `action_id`: FK to moderation_actions (nature of event).
- `actor_admin_id`: Admin [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) who performed the action, nullable if not an admin.
- `actor_moderator_id`: Moderator [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) who performed the action, nullable if not a moderator.
- `actor_member_id`: Member [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) who performed the action, nullable if not a member.
- `actor_guest_id`: Guest [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) who performed the action, nullable if not a guest.
- `action_type`: Action type for business process lookup (redundant for reportability).
- `created_at`: Entry creation timestamp (compliance/audit).
- `context`: Optional extended legal/business context (nullable for ordinary logs).

### `discussion_board_notifications`

Notification delivery audit/log. Implements notification event tracking per requirements (user feedback, moderation, and system status). Maintains 3NF by linking only by foreign keys for polymorphic recipients (admin/member/moderator/guest) and optional linkage to posts, comments, or moderation actions.
For example, when a moderator resolves a report, a notification is recorded for the affected user. Key relationships: references actors tables for recipient, content and moderation tables for context. Special behaviors: exactly one recipient per notification row (only one of admin_id, member_id, moderator_id, guest_id is non-null), delivery state changes tracked by status and timestamp fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for this notification.
- `admin_id`: Recipient admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins)
- `moderator_id`: Recipient moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators)
- `member_id`: Recipient member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members)
- `guest_id`: Recipient guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests)
- `post_id`: Associated post's [discussion_board_posts.id](#discussion_board_posts) if relevant, or null for other notification types.
- `comment_id`: Associated comment's [discussion_board_comments.id](#discussion_board_comments) if relevant, or null for other notification types.
- `moderation_action_id`: Associated moderation action's [discussion_board_moderation_actions.id](#discussion_board_moderation_actions) for moderation event notifications or null otherwise.
- `type`: Notification type ("in-app", "email", etc.) - channel-specific delivery.
- `category`: Notification category (e.g., "comment_reply", "vote", "moderation_event") - sub-type for preference filtering.
- `message`: Notification body for display in app or email.
- `is_read`: Whether the notification has been read by the recipient user.
- `status`: Delivery status: 'pending', 'sent', 'failed', etc.
- `created_at`: Time when notification was created (system event for audit).
- `delivered_at`: Timestamp when delivered/sent to the user (for lifecycle analytics).
- `read_at`: Timestamp notification was read (UI or email event).
- `error_message`: Failure explanation if delivery error occurs.

### `discussion_board_notification_settings`

User notification preference entity; implements per-user channel and category preferences per requirements. Maintains strict 3NF; all fields are atomic. Used to determine if/when to deliver notification for specified event types and channels. For example, a member can opt out of vote notifications by adjusting vote_notification_enabled. Key relationships: references actors via foreign keys; at most one settings row per user per actor type (unique constraint). Special behaviors: at most one recipient field is non-null; preference updates tracked by updated_at.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key - Unique identifier for this notification settings row.
- `admin_id`: Settings owner's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if this is for an admin.
- `moderator_id`: Settings owner's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if this is for a moderator.
- `member_id`: Settings owner's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if this is for a member.
- `guest_id`: Settings owner's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if this is for a guest.
- `in_app_enabled`: Whether user receives in-app notifications.
- `email_enabled`: Whether user receives email notifications.
- `moderation_notification_enabled`: User preference for receiving moderation event updates.
- `reply_notification_enabled`: User preference for reply notifications.
- `vote_notification_enabled`: User preference for vote notifications.
- `created_at`: When settings record was created.
- `updated_at`: Last settings update timestamp.

### `discussion_board_auth_tokens`

Authentication token records for actors, fulfilling the requirement for secure, auditable session handling and RBAC enforcement. Implements capture, status, and historical traceability of authentication tokens for any user role (admin, moderator, member, guest). Maintains 3NF - no transitive or calculated fields. Example: Used to track currently active JWTs for members and their session expiry.
Key relationships: Flexible linkage to actors (admins, moderators, members, guests) using four optional foreign keys. Special behaviors: Token uniqueness, revocation, and session-based expiration tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each authentication token record.
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if token belongs to an admin.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if token belongs to a moderator.
- `member_id`: Member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if token belongs to a member.
- `guest_id`: Guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if token belongs to a guest.
- `actor_type`: Actor role type for polymorphic association: 'admin', 'moderator', 'member', or 'guest'.
- `token`: Signed authentication token value (e.g., JWT or similar).
- `issued_at`: Timestamp of token issuance.
- `expires_at`: Expiration time of the token (nullable if unlimited).
- `revoked`: Status if token is revoked (logout or forced invalidation).

### `discussion_board_access_logs`

Comprehensive access event log for API and system compliance, implementing the requirement to store all endpoint calls, actors, results, and sources for forensics and security analytics (e.g., tracking unauthorized attempts, data export for legal reporting). Enforces 3NF; no calculated fields. Example: Used to reconstruct incident histories and perform IP-based threat analysis.
Key relationships: Optionally references actors (including guests) for mapped event context. Four optional foreign keys for different actor types. Special behaviors: Nullability for anonymous accesses; index for high-volume endpoint queries.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each access event log entry.
- `admin_id`: Admin's [discussion_board_admins.id](#discussion_board_admins) if acting user is an admin.
- `moderator_id`: Moderator's [discussion_board_moderators.id](#discussion_board_moderators) if acting user is a moderator.
- `member_id`: Member's [discussion_board_members.id](#discussion_board_members) if acting user is a member.
- `guest_id`: Guest's [discussion_board_guests.id](#discussion_board_guests) if acting user is a guest.
- `actor_type`: Role type of the actor (admin, moderator, member, guest, null if anonymous).
- `accessed_at`: Time of access event occurrence. Implements audit/compliance tracking.
- `http_method`: HTTP method of the request (GET, POST, etc.).
- `endpoint`: API endpoint or path accessed. Supports reporting, investigation, and endpoint performance analytics.
- `result`: Result of the API call (e.g., success, failure, unauthorized).
- `ip_address`: IP address of client (nullable if not recorded due to privacy/technical reasons).
- `user_agent`: User agent string of the client (nullable if not present).

It operates on the discussion_board_categories table, which is responsible for implementing the business requirement of persistent, configurable categorized discussion areas. Each record in this table represents a unique category identified by a category name, and may be associated with an optional description. Additional metadata such as creation, update, and (potential) soft deletion timestamps are included to support audit trail and compliance features. Categories are used for assigning and filtering posts and are critical for structuring discussions and managing access controls as referenced in the requirements documentation. The API does not require parameters and returns an array or paginated set of categories.
operations.description:
Fetch the entire list of discussion board categories for discovery, navigation, and assignment purposes. This endpoint provides access to all categories, including metadata such as name, optional description, creation and updated timestamps, and potential soft-deleted state (via deleted_at).

This API serves both guest and authenticated users, supporting full category browsing by any frontend needed for post creation, filtering, or category management. Guests will only see non-deleted (active) categories, while privileged users (admins or moderators) may see all, including soft-deleted ones, depending on business logic in the implementation layer.

Fetches from the discussion_board_categories table and is used in conjunction with operations like creating or editing posts, managing tags for categories, or auditing category configuration. Access to this API is broadly open for system usability, and errors may include database connectivity issues, but not permission errors unless fine-grained access control exists downstream.

operations.specification: This operation files a new content moderation/abuse report record into the discussion_board_content_reports table. Members and guests can report posts/comments for violation of community standards, illegal/harmful content, or other policy infractions. Request body must include information about reporter (inferred from login/guest session), target post/comment, reason, category, and initial status. Upon creation, the report is set as pending (or equivalent initial state) and is ready for moderation workflow. The new report is returned so UI can confirm/audit. Moderators/admins can also report for record/audit. Enforcement of field constraints (reporter, contentType, and references) is required.
operations.description:
Create a new content/abuse moderation report for the system. The request must specify who is reporting, what they are reporting (post or comment, by ID), content type, category, reason, and any other required audit fields. This endpoint is open to any authenticated or guest session wanting to report abusive content.

Security: The reporter's identity is inferred from the token/guest session rather than request body. Validation ensures all referenced posts/comments exist. Upon creation, the report is added to the moderation queue as pending/under_review.

This operation is critical for enforcing policy and community compliance on the board. Follow-up actions may trigger notifications, status updates, or linkages to moderation actions.

The endpoint should return a paginated list of tokens with filtering and sorting capabilities for audit, security, and monitoring purposes. Sensitive data such as the token value should be handled securely and exposed only where appropriate for administrative roles. Pagination and search features allow users to locate tokens based on actor role, token status, or issuance period.

Retrieve a paginated list of authentication tokens from the discussion_board_auth_tokens entity. This operation supports audit workflows, allowing security administrators to monitor active and historical authentication sessions for all user roles (admins, moderators, members, guests).

Pagination is required, and tokens should be filterable by actor_type, issued_at, revoked status, actor id, and expiration. The response will include only necessary information for session tracking and security audits, avoiding exposure of the raw token string except where role permits.

Role-based access control is enforced so that only administrators or delegated security operators can access this operation. Errors such as unauthorized access or malformed queries should be handled with clear diagnostics.

authorization.description: Has full access to manage all aspects of the board: user and post moderation, category management, feature settings, and data export.

authorization.name: moderator
authorization.description: Can moderate discussions, handle reports, delete/edit posts, suspend users, but cannot access system settings.

authorization.name: member
authorization.description: Standard authenticated user who can post, comment, upvote/downvote, report content, and edit their own contributions.

authorization.name: guest

A paginated structure representing a summary view of guest session records for the discussion board system. Used for efficiently browsing or administrating large volumes of guest entries, including basic audit-related details without sensitive data.

This summary abstraction is based on the full guest entity, but typically includes only the most important identifying and audit fields. Referenced in listing APIs, compliance dashboards, and analytics tools.

All fields in this type are drawn from the normalized columns of the discussion_board_guests Prisma table, and are documented for clarity and compliance.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ISummary.description:
A summary view object for a discussion board guest session. This type provides an overview of guest visitation: the session id, IP address, token, and entry timestamp. It is suitable for browsing listings, analytics, abuse investigations, and operational dashboards, as referenced in the project requirements.

Every property here is derived directly from a column in the discussion_board_guests schema. No sensitive data is present, and detail is limited to what's necessary for identification and summary analytics.

Used in arrays within paginated guest listings or detail expansion UIs.

guest_ip.description: IP address associated with this guest session. Used for minimal audit and abuse tracking in compliance workflows.

session_token.description: Session token or browser fingerprint associated with the guest for deduplication and basic repeat-visitor analysis.

entered_at.description: Timestamp at which the guest entered (session started, ISO8601 as generated by the database). Supports auditing and chronological browsing.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.description:
Full entity representation of a discussion board guest session. This type encompasses all attributes stored in discussion_board_guests, including session identifiers, IP address, token, timestamps, and relations.

Use cases include individual guest session drilldown, analytics, or compliance workflows. Every field corresponds 1:1 with the atomic columns in the underlying Prisma table, with special emphasis on auditability, privacy compliance, and forensics capability.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.ICreate.description:
Creation DTO for a new guest session entry. Used during guest analytics or on-boarding workflows to record the critical session identifiers. Required fields are strictly those defined in the discussion_board_guests schema; regulatory and business logic for new guest creation is enforced at the service layer.

Corresponds to guest analytics/audit policies and supports deduplication, abuse tracking, and system access logging.

guest_ip.description: IP address of the guest initiating the session; must be valid at time of session recording.

session_token.description: Session-specific token or fingerprint for tracking the guest during their access period.

Only updatable atomic fields defined in the Prisma schema for discussion_board_guests are represented here.

IDiscussionBoardPost.description:
Full, detailed representation of a discussion board post, strictly conforming to the discussion_board_posts schema fields. Contains all atomic columns as well as nullable foreign keys for threading and authorship. No sensitive data or lateral relations (votes, tags, comments) are included directly. Soft deletion is present as nullable deleted_at (for audit/moderation compliance).

All property descriptions reference the underlying Prisma schema, and status/ownership fields are present for compliance and traceability.

Ownership and soft-deletion policies are handled outside of this DTO at the service/business logic layer. This is invoked via PUT/PATCH APIs, never for creation.

IDiscussionBoardAccessLog.description:
Immutable, atomic record for a single API or system access event in the discussion board system.

Captures all relevant information for audit-trail, incident investigation, and legal compliance. All fields are atomic and normalized as per schema requirements. Exposed to only authorized roles due to sensitive/forensic nature of data.

Corresponds directly to a row in discussion_board_access_logs, and includes all direct actor linkages, access context info, timing, and method/type attributes.

id.description: Primary key for this access log entry.

Role type of the actor ('admin','moderator','member','guest', or null if unknown/anonymous).

endpoint.description: Exact API path or endpoint for this access (URI template).

IDiscussionBoardAccessLog.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating new API access log records as used by the discussion board system's logging/audit infrastructure.

Populates all atomic fields required to document a single access attempt, including actor relationship, request context, IP, time, and relevant metadata. Used internally for event recording on API call lifecycle or user authentication event. No derived/calculated data is included.

IDiscussionBoardAccessLog.IUpdate.description:
Updatable fields for existing access log records in the discussion board system.

Intended for very limited correction/annotation (e.g., fixing context/meta fields) by authorized admin actors only. Most fields in access logs are immutable, except annotation-ready meta for compliance corrections. Used according to policy for rare legal or technical remediation.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin user can successfully retrieve a paginated list of all guest session records. The test should ensure that the response contains expected guest metadata (session token, IP, timestamps). Data should include both recent and historical sessions. Only admin-level authenticated requests are permitted; attempts by non-admins or guests should be rejected by RBAC, though such negative scenarios may rely on excluded endpoints for dependency. Error scenarios should verify database connectivity handling and appropriate error responses for infrastructure failure.

Test advanced filtering and searching for guest session records. As an admin user, submit various filter queries (by IP, session token fragment, or date range) and verify the paginated, filtered results match the query. Ensure that correct results are returned for expected filter cases (e.g., a specific guest IP). Also confirm that invalid queries (e.g., malformed date ranges or non-existent session token fragments) result in proper error messages, not system failures.

dependencies.purpose: Create multiple guest sessions with varying IPs and session tokens so that filtering can be accurately tested for different values.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch full details for a single guest access session record via its guestId. The response should contain all relevant fields, including IP address, session token, and timestamps. Attempting to access a non-existent guestId should return a 404 error. Attempted access by non-admin roles should result in an authorization error (RBAC negative test), though execution of such a path may be in dependency. Confirm that proper validation and error handling occur for malformed or unauthorized requests.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new guest session so the returned guestId can be used to fetch details for a real record.

scenario.draft: Verify that a new guest session can be registered with valid IP address, unique session token, and timestamp. Confirm that after successful creation, the response contains all expected data (including guestId and timestamps), and that session records are persisted for future audit purposes. Attempt to register two sessions with the same token should not fail unless additional uniqueness rules are present. Error scenarios should test missing/invalid required fields (e.g., invalid IP, null session token), and ensure that blocked or excessive abuse attempts (rate limiting) are handled according to business policy.

Verify that as an admin, it's possible to update details on a registered guest session record (IP address, session token, or entry timestamp). The test should confirm that after updating, the record reflects the new values, and that audit logs (if accessible elsewhere) record the update. Attempt to update a non-existent guestId and confirm a 404 error is returned. Provide an invalid value for a field (e.g., non-IP string for IP address) and verify appropriate validation error. Ensure permission error is returned if attempted by a non-admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register a guest session record which can be updated as part of the admin session update test.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of a moderator user to search and filter moderation reports using different filter criteria such as reporter identity, content type, report status, category, date range, and related post/comment IDs. Verify that expected pagination, sorting, and fields are returned, and that role-based access control is enforced. Confirm that filters return only accessible reports and pagination metadata is correct. Include dependency on at least one content report being present (either by prior creation or as a prerequisite of test).

dependencies.purpose: Ensure at least one content report exists in the system for meaningful search and filtering operations.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin user can execute advanced searches for moderation/abuse reports, applying various combinations of filters (reporter identity, report status, category, referenced post or comment, date range) and pagination/sort settings. Confirm that returned data matches filter expectations, pagination metadata is correct, and only accessible reports are returned. Validate proper role-based access, error responses for invalid queries, and results aligning with complex audit and triage cases. Ensure prerequisite content reports are present in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure there are moderation reports available in the database before executing the search/filter tests.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve full detail for a specific content moderation report by ID, including all critical business and audit fields (report reason, reporter, related post or comment, status, timestamps, etc.). Confirm that proper error responses (404 not found, 403 forbidden) are returned if the report does not exist or is not accessible to the moderator. Confirm RBAC enforcement and that data matches record in the database. Requires a known content report ID present in the system.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content moderation report to fetch its details, ensuring a valid ID for the test.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve complete business and audit details for a specific moderation/content abuse report by its unique ID. Confirm that fields such as reporter, target, reason, status, category, and audit timestamps are included. Validate correct error behavior for missing or unauthorized access, and that RBAC is enforced. Dependency on having at least one moderation report present, created if needed via content report creation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report in the system for which the admin can fetch details and verify data accuracy.

scenario.draft: Test that a logged-in member can create a new content moderation (abuse) report for a given post or comment, specifying the appropriate reason, category, content reference (postId or commentId), and optional details. Confirm that the system validates referenced content, requires mandatory fields, and logs the event. On success, the created report should return full audit information. Requires that the post or comment to be reported already exist.

Attempt to create a moderation report referencing a non-existent or already deleted post/comment as a member. Verify that the system returns an appropriate error indicating missing content and does not create the report. Confirms validation of foreign key references on abuse reporting APIs.

Attempt to submit a content report as a member with missing mandatory fields such as content reference, reason, or category. Verify that the API enforces required fields and returns descriptive validation error responses, preventing incomplete submissions.

Simulate a guest reporting abusive content using this endpoint (if permitted by business logic), and confirm guest identity is extracted from session, not the payload. Results should show successful submission or appropriate restriction based on endpoint role configuration.

Verify the ability of a moderator to search and paginate the moderation actions record using different filtering criteria such as action type, actor (admin or moderator), report reference, and date range. Scenario should include filtering for a specific type of moderation action (e.g., 'suspend' or 'delete'), as well as negative cases (e.g., searching with no matching result, wrong actor id). Pagination and sorting should be covered. Moderator must have proper authentication. Error scenarios: invalid filter criteria, unauthorized user access, and exceeding page size limits.

dependencies.purpose: Create several moderation actions with different types and actors to populate the dataset for search and filtering.
Generate content reports to be referenced by moderation actions, ensuring realistic report-action linkage for filter testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific moderation action by its unique id. Test with a valid moderationActionId to ensure all relevant information (type, actor, report reference, rationale, timestamp) is returned. Also test error scenarios: access with an invalid or non-existing moderationActionId (expect 404), and request by an unauthorized role (expect 403 or similar permission error).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as an admin to ensure there is a valid record to retrieve in the main test.

scenario.draft: Ensure a moderator can access the full details of a specific moderation action using a valid ID. Test successful data retrieval, and failure scenarios such as invalid or unauthorized access: attempt retrieval with an incorrect id (expect 404), as well as as a user without appropriate permissions (expect 403/unauthorized).

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action as a moderator to have a valid moderationActionId for evaluation.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new moderation action in response to a content report, using valid input data (including actor, action type, report reference, and rationale). Confirm the record is persisted and returned with all relevant metadata. Also test duplicate or repeat attempts for the same report-action combination (may expect uniqueness handling or allow multiples per business logic). Error scenarios should include missing required fields, reference to non-existing content report, invalid role/actor, or malformed rationale.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content report to serve as the reference for the moderation action under test.

scenario.draft: Validate that a moderator can submit a new moderation action for an associated content report, supplying all required fields (action type, report reference, rationale, etc.) and that the record is created and audit-logged correctly. The scenario also covers attempts with missing or invalid data: omitting required fields, referencing an invalid or deleted content report, or providing an invalid actor. Check that the API enforces RBAC by denying creation by unauthorized roles. Success is verified by the action's existence and its relationships to the actor and report.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new content report as a prerequisite for associating a moderation action in the test.

scenario.draft: Test searching and filtering guest notifications with various criteria (category, status, type, date range). First, create a guest session using the appropriate endpoint to obtain a guestId and initiate the audit trail. Generate several notifications for that guest using the notification creation endpoint, varying the notification category, status (read/unread), and creation timestamps. Then, as the guest, apply different filter parameters (e.g., unread only, notifications of a particular category, or those delivered within a certain period) and ensure the results match the applied filters precisely, are paginated correctly, and that notifications for other users (members, admins, etc.) are not returned. Verify that unauthorized filter attempts or malformed queries yield validation errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new guest session to obtain a guestId for the notification context.
Create notification records associated with the generated guest session for subsequent searching and filtering.

scenario.draft: Test detail retrieval of an individual notification for an admin user. First, create an admin account and authenticate. Create a notification that explicitly targets this admin using the notification creation endpoint. Then, attempt to fetch this notification by its ID as the correct admin. Validate that all details are returned as per the schema. Additionally, attempt to fetch a notification belonging to another user (member/moderator/guest) to verify that access is denied (forbidden or not found). Ensure all error messages are clear and roles are strictly enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account for testing notification ownership and detail retrieval.
Create notification records linked to the admin account for detail view and permission validation.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving the detail of a single notification as a moderator. First, set up a moderator account and create at least one notification specifically for that moderator. As the moderator, retrieve the notification by its ID and confirm all fields match what was sent. Additionally, attempt to access a notification addressed to another user (admin, member, or guest) and check that access is denied or results in not found. This scenario also covers attempts to access nonexistent notifications for robust error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to receive notifications.
Create notifications scoped for the moderator to support retrieval and permission tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a notification detail as a member user. Begin by creating a member account and generating at least one notification addressed directly to that member.
