Use the advanced search endpoint to filter by member, time range, or parent ID and verify that only matching comments are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Register member(s) for comment authorship.
Create a post to attach comments.
Post a set of comments with different attributes for filtering.

scenario.draft: Test that when searching as an unauthenticated user, soft-deleted comments are excluded. Soft-delete one or more comments, then verify they do not appear in search results, even if the search criteria would otherwise include them. (This can be compared to admin/moderator behavior in separate scenarios.)

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for comment creation.
Create a post for comments.
Add several comments.
Soft-delete at least one comment.

scenario.draft: Test that the endpoint correctly returns a validation error when given bad search criteria (such as invalid page size, unsupported filter values, or malformed query data). Send an invalid request body and verify that the response describes the validation issue.

Test retrieving details for a valid comment by postId and commentId. Set up a post and comment as preconditions, then call this endpoint and verify that the response includes all expected fields, author, and threading info.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.
Create a post for testing.
Create a comment for lookup.

scenario.draft: Test the endpoint's response when the commentId does not exist for a valid postId. Attempt to fetch a random or deleted comment and expect the API to return a 404 or not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.
Create a post for reference.

scenario.draft: Test for the edge case where a valid commentId is provided, but the postId in the path does not own that comment. Attempt to retrieve the comment with a mismatched postId and verify that the system returns an appropriate linkage or not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.
Create at least two posts.
Create a comment on the first post.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated member can successfully add a comment to a post. Register a member, create a post, and then use the member's credentials to comment on that post. Validate that the response includes the new comment, author linkage, and timestamp.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for commenting.
Create a post to comment on.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a member attempts to create a comment on a postId that does not exist. Use an invalid UUID for postId and verify that the system returns a not-found or error response indicating the post does not exist.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account for posting and commenting.

scenario.draft: Test that a comment cannot be created by an unauthenticated user. Attempt to post a comment as a guest or without authentication and verify that the system returns an unauthorized/access denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a post as a member first, so there is a valid postId for commenting.

scenario.draft: Verify that a member who is the author of a post can search and paginate through edit history for their own post using a specific date range filter and keyword in the edit rationale. Firstly, create a verified member account and have them submit a post. Perform two separate edits with audit rationales at different dates. Next, request a PATCH search with date filters and rationale keyword, expecting the results to contain only the edits within the provided parameters. Check that the API respects authorization and returns results limited to edits authored by the requesting member.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new verified member to act as the post author.
This member will create a post that can be edited later.
The member makes at least two edit events on the post to generate audit trails for testing search and pagination.

scenario.draft: Assert that a member cannot retrieve or search the edit history of a post they did not author. First, create two distinct member accounts. One member creates and edits a post. The other attempts to search this post's edit history via PATCH. Confirm the API rejects the request due to lack of ownership or access rights, returning a suitable authorization error.

dependencies.purpose: Create two separate member accounts.
The first member submits a post and makes an edit event.

scenario.draft: Ensure that attempting to search edit history using a non-existent or malformed postId returns an appropriate error. A member makes a PATCH request with an invalid or random postId. The system must reject the request with a resource-not-found or invalid format error, adhering to business logic for ID validation. No edit events are created beforehand, as the post doesn't exist.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to authenticate before making the search request.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search and paginate the edit history of any post, regardless of author, using advanced query filters such as rationale keyword, editor, or date range. First, create one member who authors and edits a post. Then, create a moderator account. Have the moderator perform a PATCH search against the post's edit history with various filter parameters, verifying all relevant edits are retrievable. Confirm that moderator privileges allow audit across posts they do not own and that correct results and pagination are returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will author and edit a post.
Create a moderator account for post edit review.
The member submits a post and applies edits to generate a non-empty edit trail.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator receives a validation error when performing a PATCH search on post edit history with an invalid date range (end date before start date or out-of-bounds values). After creating a moderator and a post with edit history, perform a search using an incorrect date filter and expect a proper API error message for invalid input parameters.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator for the search operation.
A sample post must exist with edits to target with the invalid date range filter.

scenario.draft: Ensure an administrator can search and filter edit history of any post using the PATCH endpoint, specifying a rationale keyword. Create a post (with edits) as a member, and have an admin search for edits by rationale substring. Confirm the correct subset of edits is returned. This test also validates full access scope for admins.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member who will own the post.
Create an admin user for audit/testing.
Generate a post with at least two rationale-differentiated edits.

scenario.draft: Verify that if an admin attempts to search the edit history of a post that does not exist, the API returns a not-found error. After ensuring the admin is authenticated, invoke PATCH with a random or deleted postId. The response should correctly indicate the invalid resource.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to make the request.

scenario.draft: Confirm that the member who authored a post can fetch details for a specific edit event by its ID. Steps: Register a member, create a post, make two edits, then use GET on one postEditId. Validate the returned event is correct, belongs to the post, and contains all expected audit information.

dependencies.purpose: Create a verified member account to serve as post author.
The member creates a post to be edited.
Generate multiple post edit events for selection.

scenario.draft: Test that a member cannot access a specific post edit event they do not own. Set up two members: one creates and edits a post, the other tries to GET a post edit event from it. Expect a forbidden error response due to lack of access rights.

dependencies.purpose: Create two different member accounts.
Have the first member author and edit their post.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a post edit event using an invalid postEditId. Register a member, create a post, and then issue a GET with a random/nonexistent postEditId. Validate the API returns a not-found or bad-id error, enforcing data integrity and resource protection.

dependencies.purpose: Register a valid member before test execution.
Ensure a real post exists for ID context.

scenario.draft: Validate that a moderator can fetch the details of any post edit event, regardless of author. Set up a member and a moderator; member creates and edits a post, then moderator uses GET for a specific post edit event. Confirm that all expected details are present and access control allows this privileged operation.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member who will create and edit a post.
Create a moderator user for access testing.
The member authors and edits the post.

scenario.draft: Check that attempting to retrieve a post edit by postEditId that does not exist returns a not-found error for a moderator as well. After moderator auth, invoke GET with an invalid postEditId (either random or after deleting all edits on the post). The API should return a 404 or equivalent error, demonstrating consistent resource validation.

dependencies.purpose: Set up a moderator for test execution.

scenario.draft: Test updating a moderation action successfully as an admin. First, create a content report that will serve as the basis for a moderation action. Then, create a moderation action as an admin user referencing this report (such as issuing a warning). Next, update the moderation action's details (such as modifying the rationale or action type) using the admin endpoint. Verify the returned record reflects the new values and all audit fields are appropriately updated. This ensures only allowed fields are modifiable and immutable properties remain unchanged.

dependencies.purpose: Create an abuse/content report to serve as the context for moderation action.
Create a moderation action linked to the content report, so it can be updated in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action as a regular member or guest user and confirm that the operation is forbidden. After preparing a content report and its associated moderation action, perform an update using non-privileged credentials. Verify that access is denied with the appropriate error code, ensuring RBAC enforcement for sensitive moderation actions.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report to underpin the moderation action.
Create a moderation action for this content report to test unauthorized update attempts.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action using an unsupported or invalid action type value as an admin. After creating a valid content report and moderation action, send an update request that contains an invalid action type in the payload. The system should reject the update and return a validation error, enforcing allowed enum or const values for action types.

dependencies.purpose: Creates a content report so a moderation action may be created and tested for update.
Creates a moderation action so the invalid action type can be tested during update.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of moderation action details by a moderator user. The scenario starts by creating a content report, then a moderation action linked to the report. As a moderator, update one or more allowed fields (such as rationale or action type) and verify the update is reflected in the returned record. Confirm that only valid, mutable fields are updated, immutable data remains untouched, and all changes are audit-tracked.

dependencies.purpose: Create a content report to serve as the basis for moderation action creation.
Create a moderation action as a moderator for the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a moderation action as a moderator but omit mandatory fields from the payload. The system should reject the request and return a validation error indicating which required fields are missing. This enforces client validation and schema compliance for moderation action updates.

dependencies.purpose: Prepare a content report necessary for moderation action creation.
Create a moderation action that will be the update target for missing data test.

scenario.draft: Ensure an admin can hard-delete a moderation action. Begin by creating a content report and a moderation action linked to it. Then as an admin, delete the moderation action by its ID. Verify the record is removed from the data source and does not appear in subsequent lists. Confirm that deletion is permanent and audit logs, if any, are updated accordingly.

dependencies.purpose: Support moderation action creation by providing a valid content report.
Create a moderation action to be deleted in this scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a moderation action with a random or already-deleted moderationActionId as an admin. The API should respond with a 404 not found error, verifying that attempts to delete non-existent records are handled gracefully and do not reveal sensitive info.

Test retrieving the list of all moderation appeals as an admin. Populate the system with at least one valid moderation action, then file an appeal referencing it as a member. As an admin, fetch the list of appeals and verify it includes the newly created record as well as any existing ones, ensuring paging, status, and rationale fields are correct.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action that can be referenced in an appeal.
File an appeal as a member referencing the moderation action for the listing scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that the appeals listing supports filtering and pagination by creating multiple appeals with varying characteristics (status, appellant, action reference). Use query or request parameters to filter the appeal list and paginate results. Confirm correct records are returned in each page and filters accurately limit results based on search criteria.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least two moderation actions as context for multiple appeal creation.
File multiple appeals against the available moderation actions to test pagination and filtering.

scenario.draft: Ensure a moderator can retrieve all moderation appeals. First, create at least one moderation action and submit an appeal linked to it from another user (member or guest). As a moderator, list all existing appeals and verify that appeal records and necessary relationships (actor, status, action reference) are present and correct in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderation action to serve as context for an appeal.
Submit an appeal as a member referencing the given moderation action for listing.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve appeals as a guest or regular member (not moderator/admin). The API should return a forbidden error, denying access to the appeals endpoint to unauthorized roles. This tests access control and ensures sensitive appeal data is restricted to privileged staff.

Test successful creation of a new vote (upvote) on a comment by a valid, active, authenticated member. Steps: Register a new member, create a post, then add a comment as the member. Finally, as the logged-in member, submit an upvote for the comment. Expect success response and audit of the voting action.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member for authentication and comment/vote actions.
Create a post to associate with the test comment and support later comment voting.
Add a new comment as the member; required as voting is only possible on existing comments.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a duplicate vote fails for the same member and comment. Steps: Register and authenticate a member, create a post and a comment, then submit an upvote for the comment. Attempt to create another vote (upvote or downvote) on the same comment by the same member. Expect a validation error due to unique vote constraint.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member able to vote and comment.
Create a post so a comment and vote may be created.
Create a comment that can be voted on by the member.
Cast the initial vote for the comment to test duplicate constraint on second attempt.

scenario.draft: Test that unauthenticated (guest) users cannot vote on comments. Steps: Create a member and a comment as setup. Then, attempt to post a vote on the comment without authenticating as a member. Expect permission error/denial for the vote creation attempt.

scenario.draft: Test the successful retrieval of all access logs as an admin user. Test the failure scenario when a non-admin user attempts to retrieve access logs. The API should reject unauthorized access and return the appropriate permission error. This ensures sensitive log data cannot be accessed by users without admin privileges.

Test handling of access log retrieval when the database is unavailable or a backend error occurs. The system should return a meaningful error response without leaking sensitive server information. Robust error handling is essential for reliability and security.

Test submitting an invalid or malformed search request (such as wrong field names or bad data types) and validate that the system responds with clear validation error messages. This ensures query robustness against client-side integration errors.
Test that the PATCH search of access logs cannot be invoked by non-admin users. Verify that permission is enforced at the API layer and unauthorized requests are rejected as per policy.

Test creating a new access log entry in response to a backend or administrative operation. All required fields (actor, endpoint, http_method, result, timestamp, etc.) must be supplied. Test failure on access log creation with incomplete or missing required fields. Validate that the API returns clear validation errors and that the partial or malformed records are not created. This enforces data integrity for system audit logs.

Test that only system services or authorized admin actors can create access log entries directly. If a non-authorized entity attempts to create a log entry, the operation should be rejected with a permission error, maintaining audit reliability and preventing forged audit records.

Test updating a mutable field of an existing access log record (such as correcting context or linked actor) as an admin. The operation should succeed only for fields allowed by the schema and business policy, and the response must reflect the new updated record. Changing immutable or forbidden fields must not be allowed, as this is critical for audit trustworthiness.

Seed the system with enough reported content (at minimum multiple posts with reports) to span several pages, then fetch the paginated list as a moderator. Validate pagination fields reflect total, current page, and navigation info accurately.

dependencies.purpose: Register several (more than the default pagination limit) members.
Each member creates a distinct post.
Each post is reported by a different member or guest.

scenario.draft: Test that accessing the moderation report listing endpoint without moderator or admin role fails. Prepare a member, have the member attempt to access the moderation report listing, and verify that the system denies access and returns an appropriate permission or authentication error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a single member account.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch the complete content report list, including all reported posts and comments regardless of status or privacy. Set up at least one reported post and one reported comment, then have an admin retrieve the entire content report set. Ensure correct data, status, and metadata visibility for regulatory and workflow compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members.
First member creates a post.
Second member comments on the post.
A report is filed for both a post and a comment.

scenario.draft: Test that when a new moderation report is created, it appears in the admin's full report list. First, generate a post, report it, then retrieve reports as admin. Confirm the new report is present, status is correct, and all IDs/fields match expectations for fresh moderation flow audits.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member.
Member creates a post.
File an abuse report for the post.

scenario.draft: Test that non-admin users cannot access the admin content report endpoint. Attempt to retrieve the content report listing as a regular member and verify access is denied, with a clear error indicating insufficient permissions.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member user.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an admin to search and paginate board settings records using valid search criteria. The test should cover filtering by title, enabled status, created or updated date ranges, and partial matches on board descriptions. Verify that the search returns paginated, filtered results matching only those records that meet the provided criteria. This scenario ensures that the backend supports efficient configuration management and analytics by admins.

dependencies.purpose: Create several board settings records with diversified attributes to cover cases for search filtering (e.g., various titles, enabled/disabled, and dates).

scenario.draft: Test search and pagination of board settings with criteria that are designed to produce no matching records. For example, use a random string as the board title or a date range outside the existing records. The system should return an empty results page. This validates that the search mechanism gracefully handles empty result sets and user error scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create board settings records as setup to ensure that there are known records in the database, ensuring that the filter used will intentionally produce zero results.

scenario.draft: Attempt to access the search board settings endpoint as a non-admin user (e.g., member or guest). The system should reject the request with a permission error, preventing unauthorized access to administrative configuration data. This scenario enforces security and proper RBAC on sensitive admin-level data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a normal member account to use for simulating a permission error when calling the admin search endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test successful retrieval of an existing board settings configuration by its unique ID. The scenario should verify that all fields (title, enabled/disabled, description, logo_uri, timestamps, etc.) match what was provided at creation. This ensures admins can drill down into specific configuration data as required for editing or compliance audit.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board settings record and extract its ID for use in the detail retrieval step.

scenario.draft: Attempt to retrieve a board settings record using a non-existent or deleted ID. The system should return a 404 error, confirming the endpoint handles not found conditions properly and does not leak sensitive information or internal errors.

Attempt to retrieve a board settings record by ID as an unauthorized user (e.g., member or guest). The endpoint should respond with a permission error (403), demonstrating correct RBAC enforcement for sensitive configuration data.

dependencies.purpose: Register a normal member account to simulate unauthorized access to the admin board setting detail endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a board configuration record by an admin with all required and optional fields (title, status, description, logo_uri, etc.). Verify that the returned record includes all input data, and that audit fields like created_at are present. This validates the main onboarding and branding use case for new boards.

Test that creating a board settings record with a title that already exists results in a validation or uniqueness error. This protects against accidental configuration collisions and enforces data integrity business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Create an initial board settings record with a given title to establish the conflict condition.

scenario.draft: Attempt to create a board settings record omitting one or more required fields (e.g., missing title or status). The system should reject the request with a validation error, confirming the backend enforces proper input validation.

Attempt to create a board settings record as a user without the admin role (e.g., member or guest). The API should return a permission error, ensuring that only authorized admins can initialize board configurations.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member or guest user to simulate unauthorized board settings creation.

scenario.draft: Test the successful update of an existing board settings record by its ID with new values for mutable fields (title, description, logo, enabled/disabled, etc.). Verify that the returned object reflects all intended changes, and that the updated_at timestamp is refreshed. This covers admin-led maintenance, brand refreshes, and compliance policy changes.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board settings record to provide a valid ID and initial state for the update scenario.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a board settings record using a non-existent ID. The system should return a 404 error, showing that updates to non-existent resources are safely handled.

Attempt to update a board settings record with invalid input data (e.g., empty title, overly long description, or unsupported logo URI format). The endpoint should reject the change and return a validation error, ensuring only valid updates are permitted.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board settings record to test invalid update inputs (e.g., set up initial state, then attempt to update with bad values).

scenario.draft: Test that updating the board setting's title to a value that matches another existing record triggers a uniqueness or business rule error. Verifies data integrity constraints and enforces unique branding.

dependencies.purpose: Create two board settings records with different titles. Then attempt to update the second record's title to match the first, leading to a conflict.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a board settings record as a user who is not an admin. The API should reject the operation with a permission error, protecting admin-only configuration from unauthorized edits.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board settings record as admin for later update attempt.
Register a member or guest user to simulate unauthorized board settings update.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully delete a board settings record by its unique ID. The scenario should verify that the record is removed from subsequent searches and retrievals and that system audit logs are updated. This ensures proper handling of configuration lifecycle and system cleanup.

dependencies.purpose: Create a board settings configuration to be deleted during the test.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a board settings record using a non-existent ID. The system should return a 404 error, demonstrating graceful handling of invalid deletion requests without system-level errors.

Attempt to delete a board settings record as a member or guest (non-admin). The endpoint should respond with a permission error, confirming that configuration deletion is restricted to administrators only.

dependencies.purpose: Create a record to attempt deletion by a non-admin user.
Register a member or guest account to simulate lack of delete privilege.

scenario.draft: Simulate an admin or moderator updating a member's active suspension to 'expired' after a successful appeal or the end of the suspension period. Ensure that the previously active ban is marked as expired, audit fields are updated, and that all compliance trails are maintained. Verify errors are returned if an unauthorized user attempts the operation, or if the update payload contains invalid fields or values. Edge cases include trying to update a non-existent suspension or passing an invalid status value.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new suspension (ban) as a prerequisite so there is a record to update.

scenario.draft: Attempt to update a suspension record as a moderator using fields not permitted by the schema (such as immutable IDs or creation timestamps), or with invalid values. The API should validate input and reject unauthorized updates, returning proper validation error messages, and not alter audit trails or immutable record fields.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure an existing valid suspension exists for which to attempt an invalid update.

scenario.draft: An administrator hard-deletes a suspension (ban) record by its UUID. Start with a created suspension, then verify that after a valid admin deletion, the record is gone (cannot be fetched by GET), audit logs are created, and all related references are handled properly. If a non-admin attempts the operation or the suspensionId does not exist, verify correct error handling (e.g., forbidden or not found).

dependencies.purpose: Create a suspension record to enable the admin to test the delete functionality.

scenario.draft: Try to delete a suspension by providing a UUID that does not correspond to any suspension in the system. The admin should receive a not-found error and no side effects should result from the action.

An admin retrieves a paginated list of audit log entries for moderation actions and compliance visibility. The scenario includes verifying that the logs are correctly paginated, only contain fields defined in the schema, and that filtering by page size or offset returns the expected subset of logs. Validate that only users with admin permissions can access this data, and unauthorized requests are rejected with clear errors. Edge cases include empty logs, page overflow, or excessively large page requests.

dependencies.purpose: Create at least one audit log entry to ensure logs exist for listing; may also relate to running test scenarios for ban/suspension update or delete actions as they generate audit logs.

scenario.draft: Test advanced searching and filtering on the audit logs endpoint as an admin. Provide complex search criteria such as filtering by specific actor, action type, or timestamp range. Ensure that only matching audit logs are returned, and that pagination and ordering work as intended. Confirm correct error handling occurs when search parameters are invalid or overly broad. Unauthorized access should be tested to ensure non-admins cannot exploit this endpoint.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure sufficient audit log data exists to search against; may relate to running admin operations that auto-generate audit logs.

scenario.draft: Retrieve the details of an individual audit log event by its unique ID. Validate that returned data matches the schema, that only authorized admin users can access it, and that not-found or forbidden errors are returned when appropriate (such as when accessing another user's log or a non-existent entry).

dependencies.purpose: Create a specific audit log entry for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test that a member who is the author of a post can successfully remove a tag from their post. The scenario starts with creating a member account and logging in. The member creates a post, assigns a tag to the post, and then attempts to delete the post-tag association via this endpoint. Confirm that the tag is removed and the association no longer appears in tag queries for that post.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account for authorization and to represent post authorship.
Create a new post as the test author member.
Create a new tag for assignment, requires admin privileges to create tags.
Assign the tag to the newly created post before testing the deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that a member who is not the author of a post cannot remove a tag from that post. Two member accounts are created. The first member creates a post and assigns a tag. The second member logs in and attempts to delete the post-tag association. The system should respond with an authorization failure, and the tag association remains intact.

dependencies.purpose: Create two separate member accounts, one to author the post, one to try unauthorized deletion.
Create a post as the first member (the author).
Create a tag as admin (only admins may create tags).
Assign the tag to the post as the author before testing unauthorized removal.

scenario.draft: Test deletion of a post-tag association that does not exist. Attempt to delete a tag assignment using a random or non-existent postTagId for an existing post. Confirm that the operation returns a not-found or appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member account to perform the operation.
Create a post as the member, required for referencing the path.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to remove a tag from a post that has been soft deleted returns an error. Flow: Member creates account, creates post, assigns tag, then soft deletes the post (via the post deletion endpoint). Attempt to delete the postTag association and confirm that the operation fails with a proper error indication because the parent post is soft deleted.

dependencies.purpose: Create member for test execution.
Create the post for association.
Create the tag to assign (admin only).
Assign the tag to the post before deletion.
Soft-delete the post so the tag removal occurs on a deleted entity.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can remove a tag from any post, regardless of authorship. Create a member who authors a post, assign a tag. Log in as moderator and remove the tag assignment from the post. Confirm the tag is unassigned from the post successfully.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member to author the test post.
Create the post as the member.
Create a tag to assign to the post (admin action).
Assign the tag as the author prior to moderator intervention.
Create a moderator account capable of tag removal.

scenario.draft: Test moderator attempting to remove a post-tag association that does not exist, expecting a not-found error. Scenario: Moderator logs in and tries to delete a tag assignment by using a random/nonexistent postTagId. Confirm that the system returns the correct not-found error.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator for API access.
Create a post for postId path reference.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator cannot remove a tag associated with a post that has already been soft-deleted. Moderator tries to remove tag assignment after the post is deleted. Confirm the API returns an error indicating invalid operation on deleted post.

dependencies.purpose: Create moderator account for the test.
Create the post as a member for association.
Admin creates the tag to be assigned.
Assign the tag to the post.
Soft-delete the post before the tag removal attempt.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin may remove any tag association from any post, regardless of authorship or post status (so long as post exists and is not soft-deleted). Admin creates a tag, member creates a post, assigns tag, admin deletes the tag association. Confirm deletion is successful and reflected in subsequent post-tag lookups.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin account with tag deletion privileges.
Create a member to author the post.
Member creates a post.
Admin creates a tag.
Author assigns tag to the post prior to admin deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that attempting to delete a post-tag association by postTagId that does not exist returns a not found error. Admin logs in and then attempts to delete a non-existent tag assignment by specifying random postTagId and a valid postId. Expect standard not-found response as per API contract.

dependencies.purpose: Create admin account for privileged removal.
Create a post as member for postId reference.

scenario.draft: Test that the administrator cannot remove a tag from a post that has been soft-deleted. Flow: Member creates a post, assigns a tag, soft deletes the post; admin then tries to remove the tag association and expects an error indicating operation on a deleted post is invalid.

dependencies.purpose: Create the admin for tag deletion attempt.
Create a member to author the post.
Member creates the post.
Admin creates a tag.
Assign tag to the post.
Soft-delete the post before tag removal.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can query category assignments for a post they did not author (if business logic allows, depending on privacy/visibility). Member A creates a post and assigns categories. Member B attempts to fetch category assignments via this endpoint. Confirm result matches visibility rules—may return all, limited, or error, per business policy.

dependencies.purpose: Create two member accounts, one as author and one as querying user.
Member A creates post.
Create categories to be assigned.
Assign categories to the post.

scenario.draft: Test that this endpoint returns an empty result if there are no category assignments for a post. Member creates a post but does not assign any categories; then calls the endpoint and verifies the empty response.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member for post creation.
Create a post without assigning categories.

scenario.draft: Test that fetching category assignments for a post that has been soft-deleted returns either an error or an empty set. Member creates and deletes a post, then attempts to fetch the post's categories. Verify API follows business logic—ideally returns error indicating the post is deleted, or returns no assignments.

dependencies.purpose: Create member for post lifecycle.
Create the post.
Soft-delete the post before calling GET postCategories.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can use advanced search, filtering, and pagination over category assignments for their post. Scenario: Member creates post, assigns multiple categories, then issues PATCH with filters (such as by category name or assignment date) and verifies that only matching assignments are returned, with correct pagination information.

dependencies.purpose: Create the test member for authorship.
Member creates post.
Admin creates multiple categories to be used in assignments.
Assign the created categories to the post for filtering.

scenario.draft: Test that searching category assignments with filters that do not match any assignments yields an empty result. Example: Member assigns category A, then searches with filter for category B or an unassigned category, and verifies an empty set is returned.

dependencies.purpose: Create member to simulate post author.
Member creates new post.
Admin creates at least two categories (only one will be assigned).
Assign only the first category; leave the other unassigned for search test.

scenario.draft: Test that advanced search against category assignments for a soft-deleted post returns an error. Scenario: Member creates and deletes post, then attempts PATCH search on assignments, expecting an error or appropriate empty response due to post deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Create member for lifecycle simulation.
Create post to be deleted.
Soft-delete the post before performing PATCH search.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated member can retrieve a list of their notifications, verifying the correct messages and metadata are returned according to their activity (such as post replies, votes, or moderation events). The member should see only their own notifications, and the structure should match expected notification types and status (e.g., read/unread).

dependencies.purpose: Register or ensure existence of a member account required to authenticate and own notifications.

Retrieves the notifications to validate the result after activity. Notification creation happens as a consequence of business actions like posts, comments, or interactions, not by direct posting to a notifications endpoint, so the test should simulate those business actions instead of calling a non-existent POST endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test the scenario where a newly registered member has no notifications. Ensure the API correctly returns an empty result set and the structure conforms to the paginated notification schema. This confirms proper handling of the no-notification edge case for new members.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new member with no activity triggering any notifications. Use this member to test the empty inbox scenario.

scenario.draft: Test that a guest or unauthenticated user cannot access member notifications and receives an appropriate permission or authentication error. This verifies the RBAC enforcement for private notification access.

dependencies.purpose: Simulate or create a guest session. The guest will then attempt to invoke the member notifications endpoint.

scenario.draft: Verify that a guest user can retrieve notifications addressed to their session (e.g., system information, moderation results for reports submitted as a guest). The guest should only see notifications where their session is the intended recipient, matching by guest_id. Pagination and message details should conform to schema.

dependencies.purpose: Create or simulate a guest session for which notifications may be generated through activity or system events.
Active guest notifications arise from prior system actions or moderation responses, which should be implied in the test setup rather than created through a POST endpoint that does not exist.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of notifications for a guest session which has never had any notification sent to it. Confirm the endpoint returns an empty result set, properly paged and schema-conformant, for a new or inactive guest session.

dependencies.purpose: Establish a new guest session/token for which no notifications exist.

scenario.draft: Test filtering and pagination of notifications for an admin user by status (e.g., unread). Admin logs in and issues a PATCH request with search/filter criteria to only retrieve unread notifications. Assert that results include only matching notifications and pagination metadata is correctly set. This checks both filtering logic and admin-specific notification delivery.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to perform the search.

scenario.draft: Test searching notifications with an invalid filter parameter (such as an unsupported category or malformed date). The API should return a validation error, and the response should clearly indicate what is wrong with the filter request.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to invoke the notification search endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test a moderator searching notifications by category (e.g., moderation, system, or reply). The moderator issues a PATCH request to filter on a specific category, and the results should be accurately scoped and paginated, showing only relevant notifications.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account for the search scenario.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator cannot search for notification records belonging to another user (admin, member, or guest). When attempting to search using another user’s identifier or filter, the API should return a forbidden or error response, protecting privacy and RBAC boundaries.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account for testing.
Register a standard member whose notifications the moderator should not access.

scenario.draft: Test member-initiated search/filtering of their own notifications by read/unread status via PATCH. After receiving several notifications, the member filters for only unread ones and verifies the endpoint only returns expected results, including empty if all are read. Also test with no matching notifications for specific status.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account and log in.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can search their notifications by type (e.g., reply, vote) and paginate through large result sets. Multiple notifications across types are created, then the member applies a filter by type and requests a specific page of results. The endpoint should respond with accurate type-filtered, paginated results and total count.

dependencies.purpose: Create a member and authenticate.

import { MyGlobal } from "../MyGlobal";
import typia, { tags } from "typia";
import { Prisma } from "@prisma/client";
import { v4 } from "uuid";
import { toISOStringSafe } from "../util/toISOStringSafe";
import { IDiscussionBoardSuspension } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/IDiscussionBoardSuspension";
import { ModeratorPayload } from "../decorators/payload/ModeratorPayload";

/**
 * Create a new suspension or ban record (discussion_board_suspensions).
 *
 * This operation is used to impose a new suspension or ban, fulfilling both
 * business logic (discipline, compliance) and technical requirements for
 * auditability. Payload must include all atomic details as per Prisma model:
 * subject (actor being suspended/banned), actor (admin/moderator imposing),
 * start time, reason, and any optional linkage to abuse reports or moderation
 * actions.
 *
 * On successful creation, the complete suspension record is returned, ensuring
 * that immediate audit and notification requirements can be met. Security
 * requirements are enforced: Only administrators or moderators can create
 * suspensions/ban records; invalid or incomplete bodies are rejected.
 * Soft-deletion or update of suspensions is handled by other endpoints.
 *
 * Related operations include update, GET-by-id/detail, and erase endpoints.
 * Error management covers permission, field validation, and
 * duplicate-checking.
 *
 * @param props - Function input containing moderator (ModeratorPayload) and
 *   body (ICreate suspension/ban details)
 * @param props.moderator - Authenticated moderator performing this operation
 * @param props.body - Details for the new suspension/ban event
 * @returns Newly created, full suspension/ban record
 * @throws {Error} If creation fails in the database layer
 */
export async function post__discussionBoard_moderator_suspensions(props: {
  moderator: ModeratorPayload;
  body: IDiscussionBoardSuspension.ICreate;
}): Promise<IDiscussionBoardSuspension> {
  const { moderator, body } = props;
  const id = v4() as string & tags.Format<"uuid">;
  const created = await MyGlobal.prisma.discussion_board_suspensions.create({
    data: {
      id,
      suspended_admin_id: body.suspended_admin_id ?? null,
      suspended_moderator_id: body.suspended_moderator_id ?? null,
      suspended_member_id: body.suspended_member_id ?? null,
      suspended_guest_id: body.suspended_guest_id ?? null,
      admin_id: body.admin_id ?? null,
      moderator_id: moderator.id,
      related_report_id: body.related_report_id ?? null,
      related_action_id: body.related_action_id ?? null,
      suspended_at: toISOStringSafe(body.suspended_at),
      ends_at: body.ends_at ? toISOStringSafe(body.ends_at) : null,
      reason: body.reason,
      status: body.status,
    },
  });
  return {
    id: created.id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">,
    suspended_admin_id: created.suspended_admin_id
      ? (created.suspended_admin_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    suspended_moderator_id: created.suspended_moderator_id
      ? (created.suspended_moderator_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    suspended_member_id: created.suspended_member_id
      ? (created.suspended_member_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    suspended_guest_id: created.suspended_guest_id ?? null,
    admin_id: created.admin_id
      ? (created.admin_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    moderator_id: created.moderator_id
      ? (created.moderator_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    related_report_id: created.related_report_id
      ? (created.related_report_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    related_action_id: created.related_action_id
      ? (created.related_action_id as string & tags.Format<"uuid">)
      : null,
    suspended_at: toISOStringSafe(created.suspended_at),
    ends_at: created.ends_at ? toISOStringSafe(created.ends_at) : null,
    reason: created.reason,
    status: created.status as "active" | "expired" | "revoked",
  };
}
